h1: Mor Mor Resort Ang Thong — rice-field garden bungalows, quiet, breakfast included, park at your door
intro: If you want a place in Ang Thong where you wake up to green rice fields, clean air and real quiet rather than a building in town, Mor Mor Resort (Mor Mor Resort Ang Thong) is a small 4-unit resort in Pa Ngiw, Mueang Ang Thong, that lovers of a rural setting talk about. The rooms are single-storey bungalows spread through a garden, with a fish pond, a vegetable plot, an evening sala and even a small museum of old household items to wander. A complimentary breakfast is provided, you can park right outside your door, and rates from about ฿950/night make it an easy pick for a slow, nature-side break on a modest budget.

body.html: What sets Mor Mor Resort apart from an in-town block is its genuinely rural, rice-field setting. The resort is just 4 single-storey houses spread through a garden ringed by greenery and paddy, where you park right outside your door. Around it are a fish pond, a vegetable plot and a sala to sit in and catch the evening breeze, plus a small museum of old household items for a wander. Real reviews repeatedly mention the quiet, the clean air, and the way a light mist settles over the resort on rainy-season mornings.

On location, be honest with yourself: this is a rural resort built for self-drivers. It sits at 39 Moo 6, Pa Ngiw, near Highway 4017, about 7 km from the Nai Dok Nai Thong Kaew Monument, with central Ang Thong a short drive away. It suits travellers who want to escape the bustle and sleep to the sound of nature, or use it as a base touring Ang Thong and Ayutthaya, more than those who want to shop or find food right outside, since walkable spots are limited and you'll need to drive out a little.

Rooms come in both double-bed and twin configurations. What real reviews consistently praise is that the rooms are clean, spacious and have comfortable beds. Each has air-con, a TV, a fridge, a desk and chairs, drinking water and a private bathroom with the basics you need for a night or two. Another thing guests like is the breakfast the resort makes for visitors — a nice extra you rarely get at a small place in this price band. With only 4 units, the owner keeps a close, friendly eye on everyone.
"Clean, spacious room, comfortable bed, quiet setting, lovely rice-field views and fresh air, friendly owner — and breakfast included. Great value for the price."

To be honest, Mor Mor Resort is a small, family-run place, not a resort with hotel-grade facilities. There's no pool, gym or all-day restaurant, and with just 4 units it fills up fast on long weekends and holidays, so it's worth calling ahead. Most bookings are made by phone or through the resort's Facebook page directly, and rates on some channels shift with promotions and the season. Anyone expecting big-resort service should reset expectations to the level of a warm, clean house in a garden.

Overall Mor Mor Resort earns praise at around 8.0 out of 10 from real guest reviews, rating especially well for cleanliness, atmosphere and value. It isn't a luxury resort, but measured on quiet bungalows, rice-field views, a fish pond and sala, an included breakfast, easy parking and a starting rate near ฿950 (rising a little by season), it does the job of a nature-side stay in Ang Thong nicely on a comfortable budget — a good fit for couples, small families and travellers who want calm more than a full set of facilities.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Mor Mor Resort Ang Thong

faq.q: Where is Mor Mor Resort in Ang Thong, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Mor Mor Resort is at 39 Moo 6, Pa Ngiw, Mueang Ang Thong, near Highway 4017. It's about 7 km from the Nai Dok Nai Thong Kaew Monument, roughly a 12-minute drive into central Ang Thong, with Wat Muang and Ayutthaya an easy onward drive.

faq.q: How much does Mor Mor Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from about ฿950/night. There are both double-bed and twin rooms across 4 units, with prices rising a little by promotion and season — compare a few channels and ask about breakfast before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Mor Mor Resort?
faq.a: Rooms are single-storey bungalows in a garden with rice-field views, parking at your door and a quiet feel. Each has air-con, a TV, a fridge, drinking water, a desk and a private bathroom. Real reviews consistently say the rooms are clean, spacious and have comfortable beds.

faq.q: Does Mor Mor Resort include breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — the resort makes breakfast for guests, which is something many real reviews single out. It's worth asking at booking whether it's included in the room rate or an add-on so you can plan your morning.

faq.q: Does Mor Mor Resort have parking?
faq.a: Yes — free parking, and you can park right outside your room because they're single-storey bungalows in a garden. It's ideal for self-drivers with plenty of luggage, with no long walk involved.

faq.q: Who is Mor Mor Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a good fit for couples, small families and anyone wanting to sleep close to nature with rice-field views on a modest budget. It isn't about luxury or full facilities, but the rooms are clean, breakfast is included, the setting is quiet and parking is easy.
